changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6681-declared-lazy-marketplace-routes.md`

- names `views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Both marketplace chunks were held by CHUNK CO-TENANCY, not by any import of the page: rolldown had parked `components/SuggestedBindingsPanel.tsx` (statically imported by the eager `views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx`) in the first, and `console/marketplace/InstalledListWidget.tsx` (bare-imported by the package barrel for its SDUI registration) in the second. An `app-shell-eager-leaves` group in `apps/console/vite.config.ts` isolates those co-tenants so the three declared-lazy pages chunk by their own dynamic-only reachability. The console eager closure moves 3180.2 KB → 3171.5 KB gzipped (−8,888 bytes, 48 → 45 eager chunks) with the three per-chunk ceilings unmoved.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `1ccb5ba7d` (merge-base with origin/main): 3 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1870 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2482 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36801427351)

The **eager closure** is every chunk the entry reaches through static imports — what the browser fetches and parses before the app renders. The entry chunk on its own is a small fraction of it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dcf891b9e151bae3177a7f7e7b9373f3b9862e51`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card objectui#11281 (body and its three comments: triage `5921147097`, claim `5922433579`, dev report `5922924745`), PR objectui#11305 (body, file list, net diff `5f2d9676c9..dcf891b9e1`, one commit, merge-base with `origin/main` is `5f2d9676c9`), the check-runs on the head, objectui#9217's ruling B (`5919298624`), PR objectui#11271's patch (the Setup precedent), and the producer read at objectstack `origin/main` `f8178ffece` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts`, `packages/spec/src/automation/flow-trigger-kind.ts`). Four files, +331 / -11, as the report says.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The status map keeps `triggerType` and `reason`** — RIGHT. `flowRailState(s)` keeps `enabled: s.enabled !== false`, `bound: !!s.bound`, then each of `triggerType` / `reason` only when `typeof x === 'string'` and `x.length` is non-zero, spread in as `{ x }` and otherwise `{}`. That is the same narrowing `joinPackagedFlows` uses for `reason` in PR objectui#11271 (read in its patch), and it leaves the key absent rather than `undefined`-valued, the way the engine omits it. The map loop is `map[s.name] = flowRailState(s)` on the same `_status` answer the pillar already fetched; the pillar's flow load and save paths (PR objectui#11296) are not in the diff.

2. **`triggerType` absent means "no declared trigger"** — RIGHT, and it is the contract's reading, verified at the producer. The spec's `FlowRuntimeState.triggerType` is "Declared trigger type, when the flow declares one", and `bound` says "`triggerType` distinguishes the two". In the engine, `getFlowRuntimeStates()` sends `triggerType: resolved?.triggerType`; `resolveTriggerBinding` goes through `deriveTriggerBinding`, which answers `undefined` when the spec's `resolveFlowTriggerKind` does — a `screen` flow, or an `autolaunched` flow started by hand or from a screen — so `JSON.stringify` drops the key; otherwise it answers one of `record_change` / `time_relative` / `schedule` / `api` (the array-form diagnostic route also answers `record_change`). No `manual` or `screen` value exists on the wire. The dev's measurement that PR objectui#11271 has no `triggerType` reading to copy is also right: its `FlowRuntimeStateRow` reads only `name`, `enabled` and `reason`. The dot never compares `triggerType` to a value; it tests presence only, so "no trigger (run manually)" is said exactly when the row has no `triggerType`. The dev read the producer at `157baa75f2`; between that and `f8178ffece` `automation-service.ts` is unchanged and the engine.ts drift does not touch the logic of the three functions (comment edits in the `time_relative` / `schedule` cases, and unrelated packaged-flow ownership hunks).

3. **A `reason` is rendered verbatim, never parsed or compared, with no error styling** — RIGHT. The title expression is `!enabled ? offTitle : bound ? onBound : reason ? reason : triggerType ? enabled : onUnbound`. The only operation on `reason` is a presence test (the ruling's own "styles on the key's presence"); nothing in the diff matches, slices or compares it, and no platform sentence appears in source, test or changeset (both test files use a fixture string that says so). The JSX below the title is untouched: the dot's class still follows `enabled` alone (`bg-emerald-500` or `bg-muted-foreground/40`), the visible text is still `engine.studio.auto.on` / `off`, no `role=alert`, no destructive class. The Acceptance note that the title is the bare reason with no "Enabled ·" prefix is accepted: Setup pairs its "On" badge with the bare sentence, and a prefix would need a composed string or a new key, both of which the ruling forbids.

4. **A declared trigger with no `reason` gets the existing `engine.studio.auto.enabled` key** — RIGHT, honest, and the right choice over the old text. "Enabled" (`已启用` in zh; both rows exist at the head) is true of that row and claims nothing about the binding, which is what the Setup page's "On"-only badge does for the same row. The old `onUnbound` text would state the one thing the contract says `bound: false` with a `triggerType` cannot mean. No new vocabulary was added, as triage and the ruling require. The branch is reachable only from a backend that sends `triggerType` but predates `reason` (a spec older than 17.5.0): at `origin/main`, `describeUnboundReason` returns a sentence on every branch for an enabled, unbound flow that declares a trigger (policy, declined-subflow, registered-but-failed, not-registered).

5. **Older backend and manual flow render as today** — RIGHT. A row with neither field reaches `onUnbound` exactly as before; the pre-existing tooltip test (`{ enabled: true, bound: false }` titled `/no trigger/`) still pins it and is unchanged. Bound and disabled flows keep `onBound` / `offTitle`, since those checks come first.

6. **Pins** — present and consistent. `FlowStatusDot.test.tsx` adds five: the policy-unbound schedule flow's title equals its reason in en and in zh and is not `onUnbound`; the no-`triggerType` control still gets `onUnbound`; a declared trigger with no reason gets `engine.studio.auto.enabled`; bound and disabled keep `onBound` / `offTitle`. The assertions name locale keys, not English copy. `StudioDesignSurface.railUnboundReason-11281.test.tsx` adds two through the real `AutomationsPillar` with a routing `_status` double (404 on any other URL, `afterEach` asserts the route was hit): the policy flow's rail dot is titled with the reason and still reads "On"; the manual, bound and disabled rows keep their titles. Both of the card's pins and all three controls are present. The red-first arithmetic holds: the four pins that cannot pass at the branch point are the two reason pins, the declared-no-reason pin and the pillar policy pin; the seven green are the four existing tests and the three controls. The ablation claim is also the only shape it could take: removing the two spreads in `flowRailState` can redden only a pin that goes through the map, which is the pillar policy pin, while the dot's unit pins hand it state directly. Neither run was repeated here (read-only); the head's Test shards are the gate. The pillar test's imports resolve at the head (`__tests__/emptyDataSource` exports `createEmptyDataSource` and `failOnAbsorbedFetchError`; `packages-io` exports `fetchPackages`), and its `useMetadata` mock matches the shape forty sibling suites use.

7. **Public surface** — none changes. `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` re-exports only `StudioDesignSurface` and `type StudioDesignSurfaceProps` from `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` (lines 436–438), and `package.json` `exports` carries only `.` and `./styles.css`, so `FlowStatusDot`'s module-level `export` is not a package surface. `FlowRailState` and `flowRailState` are module-private. The dot's prop type widened from `{ enabled; bound }` to `FlowRailState`, a superset with two optional members, so every existing caller still type-checks. `AutomationsPillar`'s props are unchanged.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/11281-rail-unbound-reason.md` declares `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`. That is right: a bug fix in a released package (`@object-ui/app-shell` 17.6.0) takes a patch, never `skip-changeset`, and nothing an author can write or import changes (①.7). `Clause-②: no` on the PR's second line and in the claim is right for the same reason — `yes` would need at least a minor, and no exported or authorable surface moved. The changeset body copies no platform sentence (its quoted "no trigger (run manually)" is the UI's own key text) and names what moved. On the head, Changeset Declaration, Changeset Bump Policy, Changeset Claim Re-read, Changeset Fixed Group Check and Changeset Overwrite Report all concluded success.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (`deviations`), each answered:
- The pillar pin got its own file, not named in the claim: within the claim's surface ("the pillar pins", same directory). Accepted.
- `metadata-admin/i18n.ts` untouched: the claim allowed it only if a title needed a key it lacked; none did. Accepted.
- Build run through `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...'`; vitest runs merged and moved to the background; the first type-check killed by a container restart and re-run; lint narrowed to the changed files with the base-blob control: each is a process note, not a contract matter; the head's check-runs are the gate for build, type-check, lint and tests. Build & E2E and Lint concluded success.
- Commit trailers model-free, PR footer in the os-dev session-URL form: AGENTS.md precedence, no contract matter.
- Cleanup done: no action.

`open_questions`: none.

`out_of_scope_findings[0]` (also the PR's second Acceptance note), the stray `/** Automations pillar — flows: list → FlowPreview … */` doc comment directly above the `FlowRuntimeState` alias docblock: verified pre-existing at the branch point `5f2d9676c9`, two consecutive JSDoc blocks of which only the nearer attaches to the alias; cosmetic; lint on the file is the same multiset as the base. Judged an Acceptance note, not fix-in-scope: the claim's surface is `FlowStatusDot` and the status map, and widening the diff to move a stray comment is not what the card bought. Carrier none, not worth a card; fold into the next edit of that region.
